root_causes.description: The product-catalog pod stopped serving for the entire window: its server-span request rate is flat zero with no request/error logs, and its container CPU sits at ~0.001 cores (idle) versus ~0.286 for the healthy frontend. As the central leaf dependency of frontend, checkout and recommendation, its loss produced the namespace-wide span-telemetry blackout and multi-second caller timeouts with no application errors.

evidence.expected_baseline: product-catalog server request_rate > 0 (steady-state under load-generator traffic)

evidence.observed_value: mean=0.001 cores; frontend comparison sum(rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace="otel-demo",pod=~"frontend-.*"}[2m])) = mean=0.286, max=0.657
evidence.expected_baseline: ~0.1-0.3 cores while actively serving (frontend at 0.286 in same window)

evidence.observed_value: no logs found between 10:50 and 13:03 (checkout and frontend log selectors also returned no logs)
evidence.expected_baseline: continuous request/health log lines for an active product-catalog pod
p95 well under 1s; round 5s/10s durations indicate callers hanging on an unavailable dependency

root_causes.description: Alternative interpretation: a latency-injection fault against product-catalog stalls its responses so that upstream spans hang at characteristic round-number timeouts (5000ms / 10002ms) without raising error status codes, which would also suppress normal server-span throughput.

evidence.observed_value: p95_duration=17714ms; individual spans user_add_to_cart=10002ms, user_view_cart=5000ms, all status ok
evidence.expected_baseline: sub-second p95 and no multi-second round-number span durations
error_rate < 0.01; a pure latency fault yields high duration with zero error status, matching this pattern

root_causes.description: The frontend (and checkout) call product-catalog directly; with that leaf unavailable their inbound server spans drop to zero in the metric pipeline while their surviving traces show long hangs — a downstream-dependency failure propagating from product-catalog rather than a fault originating in frontend itself.

evidence.observed_value: mean=0.000 p50=0.000 p95=0.000 p99=0.000 max=0.000 (frontend server request_rate flat zero)
evidence.expected_baseline: frontend server request_rate > 0 while load-generator drives traffic
checkout error_rate < 0.01; absence of errors alongside zero throughput points to dependency unavailability rather than an in-service exception

remediation_steps: Confirm product-catalog pod health and history: kubectl get pods -n otel-demo -l app.kubernetes.io/name=product-catalog and kubectl describe pod <product-catalog-pod> to inspect restart count, termination reason and last state.

Inspect whether the pod was killed (Killing/Stopping container, SuccessfulDelete then reschedule) and whether a chaos/pod-kill fault is injected against product-catalog; stop the fault injection if present.
If the container is OOM/probe-failing, raise limits / fix readiness probe; otherwise verify the replacement pod reaches Ready and resumes serving spans before clearing the watchdog.
Validate the telemetry pipeline recovery: confirm calls_total span metrics and Loki logs resume for product-catalog, frontend and checkout, and that end-to-end trace p95 returns to sub-second.
